about.title: Glendale Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A space heater that sparks in a Brand Boulevard apartment, a tire that comes apart on the Ventura Freeway, a kitchen gadget that shatters in a way no one anticipated — product injuries in Glendale rarely give warning. What they share is a legal path that differs from an ordinary accident claim. Under California's strict liability rules, you generally do not have to show the company acted negligently. You need to show the product had a defect — in its design, in how that particular unit was built, or in the warnings and instructions that came with it — and that the defect caused your harm. The same rule can reach the manufacturer, the distributor, and the retailer on San Fernando Road that put it in your hands. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Glendale residents with an independent attorney who handles defective-product cases across Los Angeles County. Being matched costs nothing, and network attorneys work on contingency, so a fee is owed only if there is a recovery. One request: keep the product.

whyChoose.title: Why Glendale Residents Use LawProactive for Product Claims

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: In California, a defective-product claim usually turns on whether the item was unsafe by design, by a manufacturing flaw, or by missing warnings — not on whether the company meant to cut corners. The attorney you're matched with knows how to frame the case around that standard.

items.title: The Product Is the Evidence
items.desc: A broken part, a charred cord, even the box it came in can carry a case. An attorney can step in early to make sure the item is preserved and examined before anyone discards or repairs it.

items.title: More Than One Company May Owe You
items.desc: California law can hold the manufacturer, the distributor, and the Glendale store that sold the product responsible together. Your matched attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim so nothing is left on the table by accident.

items.question: A part on my car failed while I was driving on SR-134 in Glendale. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It may be both. Glendale recorded 727 injury collisions in 2025, and some of those involve a mechanical failure rather than driver error alone. If a tire, brake, airbag, or steering component gave out, the manufacturer or seller of that part may be liable under California's strict liability rules. An attorney can look at the vehicle and the crash report together to decide which claims apply.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company was negligent?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability often runs on strict liability, meaning you need to show the product was defective — in design, manufacturing, or warnings — and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company was careful or careless is usually not the deciding issue. That said, gathering the right proof still matters, which is where an attorney helps.

items.question: I still have the product but the store offered to take it back and refund me. Should I return it?
items.answer: Please hold off. Once the item leaves your possession, it may be impossible to have it inspected, and the physical product is often the strongest evidence in the case. Keep it as is, along with receipts, packaging, and any instructions. LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who will advise on preserving it before you decide anything.
